csv_project_name: DB for Chesapeake Bay Bridge Protection
csv_scope_of_work: The Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) today released a Request for Proposals (RFP) inviting qualified design-build teams to submit proposals for a project to enhance the existing protection of the main span piers on both the eastbound and westbound spans of the Chesapeake Bay Bridge. MDTA has developed a comprehensive plan to install up to 16 structures to provide protection to the piers closest to the main navigation spans that accommodate inbound and outbound vessel traffic. The initial Project scope includes the installation of structures to protect the four towers supporting the main spans of the Eastbound and Westbound Bay Bridges.
csv_disciplines_requested: Design Build/Developer, Geotechnical Engineering, Surveying/GIS/Mapping, Site Evaluation/Selection, Planning/Master Planning, Analytical/Testing Services, Public Transit Planning, Traffic Design Engineering, Transportation Planning, Urban Studies/Planning/Design

MDTA plans to install up to 16 protective structures for the piers closest to the main navigation spans carrying inbound and outbound vessel traffic. services: Design-build services for bridge protection works, including design and construction of pier protection structures; requested disciplines also include geotechnical engineering, surveying/GIS/mapping, site evaluation, analytical/testing services, traffic design engineering, and transportation-related planning support.
relevance_explanation:
- Major bridge-related project on the Chesapeake Bay Bridge with significant structural and marine interface complexity.
- Scope involves protective structures for main-span piers and towers near navigation channels, indicating demanding civil/structural engineering.
- Design-build procurement creates an entry point for structural design involvement, not only construction.
- Large stated construction value suggests substantial engineering scope and strategic importance.
- Highly relevant bridge infrastructure project, though focused on protection works rather than a new long-span bridge superstructure.
